contexts.text: No one is ever forbidden to enjoy... the pleasures... of utilities from foods and drinks.
To afford drink ( 1) = to instruct.
(Hagar) gave the boy to drink () = instruction in spiritual things. To give to drink = to instruct in truths.
The soul thirsting for drink () = a longing for truth.

I will give thy camels also to drink () = the enlightenment thence of all the scientifics in the natural man... To give to drink = to enlighten. To draw water = to instruct; thus, to give to drink = to enlighten; for enlightenment comes from instruction. AC 3102.

She made him to drink () = initiation. To give to drink has a similar signification to to drink , but to give to drink here involves a greater activity on the part of him who drinks... Thus to make to drink = to give the opportunity of receiving, which is the first of initiation.
Out of that well they watered the droves () = that knowledge is from the Word... To water, or make to drink = to be instructed.
And they watered the flock () = that doctrine is thence. To water, or make to drink = to instruct... Thus to water them = to instruct from the Word, and therefore doctrine.
Water ye the flock () = still, instruction thence for a few. To water the flock = to instruct from the Word. AC 3790.
Natural truth to its good... is like drink to food. Water or drink dilutes the food... Without water or drink, the food is not resolved into its minute parts, nor is it carried about to its use...

In the other life, man is not nourished by any natural food and drink, but by spiritual food and drink; spiritual food is good, and spiritual drink is truth; wherefore, in the Word, where bread or food is mentioned, the Angels understand spiritual bread or food, namely, the good of love and of charity; and where water or drink is mentioned, they understand spiritual water or drink, namely, the truth of faith. Hence may be evident what is the truth of faith without the good of charity. AC 5360.

Everything which serves for drink, or which is drink, as wine, milk, water, relates to truth... thus to the intellectual part... That to give to drink, and to drink, in general, is predicated of the truths which are of the intellectual part. References. And that, in special, they = the truth which is from good, or the faith which is from charity. References.
A drinking is predicated of the understanding. References.
Drinks of every kind = truths.
To water the flock of their father () = that thence they might be instructed in good. To water = to instruct. AC 6781.
Under Drink, see this reference.
Heavenly food is all the good of love and of charity; and heavenly drink is all the truth of faith from that good.
Whosoever shall give to drink a drink of cold [water] ()... A drink of cold [water] = something of truth.

Because she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her whoredom () = because by profanations of the Word, and adulterations of the good and truth of the Church, she has seduced all whom she could subject to her dominion... To make to drink of that wine = to seduce. AE 881.
On the food and drink of Spirits... The cupidities of knowing are their drink; for there is nothing they do not desire to know... Wherefore, in the Word... intelligence is called drink.
Under Drunk, see this reference, and at SE 2458. SE 3177:13.
A drink of cold [water] = to exercise charity from obedience.
Spiritual drink is all the truth which is communicated and given to man by the Lord.
In the Word, where anything of drink, or that serves for drink, is mentioned, truth is understood.
To drink wine () = to draw in falsities.
He who thirsteth for drink () = those who long for truths.
To give the people to drink of the waters () = to nourish spiritually, which is effected by instructing and teaching.
To make them drink () = to teach.
To give drink to My people () = to instruct those who long for it. AE 650:36.

Spiritual eating and drinking is instruction, reception, and appropriation. It is here said of the Lord () that He hungers and thirsts, because from Divine love He longs for the salvation of all; and of man, that they gave Him to eat, and that they gave Him to drink, which takes place when, from affection, they receive and perceive from the Lord what is good and true.

To give to drink with a drink of cold [water] = to love and teach from a little innocence... To give the little ones water to drink = to teach truth from spiritual innocence; and also to teach truths to those who are innocent.
